briefings.headline: Hunt Cantillo’s fastball; don’t chase his offspeed
briefings.message: Joey Cantillo is the high-confidence expected starter. Right-handed hitters: look for the fastball, which he allows .391 xwOBA against to righties. Heriberto Hernández has the best reported matchup at .355 expected xwOBA; Griffin Conine also has a batter edge at .341, but his samples versus LHP and pitch groups are small. Stay disciplined against Cantillo’s changeup and curveball, and make him work—he averaged 87 pitches per start and 5.1 innings per start. Watch Cade Smith, Erik Sabrowski, and Hunter Gaddis in Cleveland’s bullpen.
reminders: Hunt fastballs; do not chase the changeup or curveball.
Conine’s matchup samples versus LHP and pitch groups are small.
Make Cantillo work and stay selective.

briefings.headline: Change speeds and keep Cleveland’s lefties guessing
briefings.message: Max Meyer starts. Mix breaking pitches and offspeed to Travis Bazzana and Kyle Manzardo, and avoid predictable fastballs to left-handed hitters. Keep Chase DeLauter off balance with selective offspeed. Gabriel Arias is the warning: his matchup has a batter edge, so change the approach rather than feeding his preferred breaking-ball look. In a close late lead, use Michael Petersen and Calvin Faucher to bridge to Pete Fairbanks; Cade Gibson is limited after pitching yesterday and is for a one-batter need only.

Use selective offspeed against DeLauter; vary the look to Arias.
Preserve Gibson for a one-batter need.
